packageRules.description: Backend (Go modules). gomodTidy runs `go mod tidy` after each bump so go.sum is reconciled in the same PR. A bare version bump updates only the changed module's go.sum hashes; indirect-dep additions/removals it leaves behind would otherwise fail `go mod download` / `go mod verify` in CI and block auto-merge. postUpdateOptions is a normal repo-config option (NOT the self-hosted-only postUpgradeTasks command allowlist), so it works on the hosted Mend app.

Frontend (npm / pnpm). Override rangeStrategy to 'replace' so engines constraints (e.g. node >=24.0.0 <25.0.0) and caret ranges are only rewritten when the new version no longer satisfies them; the top-level 'bump' default would otherwise churn lower bounds on every patch.

Landing page (site/). It is its own pnpm workspace with its own lockfile and deploy cadence (landing.yml publishes site/dist to gh-pages), so it gets its own group/scope/labels instead of riding the catch-all 'frontend dependencies' rule above. Renovate has no dedicated pnpm manager: the npm manager handles pnpm, pnpm-lock.yaml and pnpm-workspace.yaml, so matchManagers stays 'npm' and matchFileNames scopes the rule to site/. Placed before the pnpm-toolchain rule below so site/package.json's 'packageManager' pnpm pin still groups into 'pnpm toolchain'. rangeStrategy 'replace' mirrors the frontend rule.
Toolchain pins managed by mise (.tool-versions, mise.toml). Covers Go, Node, pnpm, supabase CLI, python, ansible-core, rust, mprocs.
Bundle the Go toolchain pin in mise (.tool-versions) with the 'go' directive in backend/go.mod into a single PR, so they cannot drift apart between CI (mise-action) and the module graph.

Bundle the pnpm pin in mise (.tool-versions) with the packageManager field in root package.json into a single PR. Vercel reads packageManager (no mise on Vercel), CI reads .tool-versions; both must move together.
Auto-merge minor and patch updates after CI passes

GitHub Actions require human review for any update. Actions execute in CI with secrets in scope, so a compromised maintainer publishing a malicious patch would otherwise auto-merge. CVE-flagged updates already bypass automerge via vulnerabilityAlerts; this rule extends that to all GHA updates regardless of severity flag.

Toolchain (mise) bumps require human review. Runtime version changes (Go, Node, pnpm, supabase CLI) can shift build/test behavior even on patch releases and propagate into CI via .tool-versions, so a bad bump can break every workflow at once.
Pin Go toolchain bumps for manual review
